title: I Was Reincarnated as a government employee with a suspicious sword in a World Where Paperwork Is Magic
synopsis: A dungeon manager tries to reduce adventurer complaints while an ancient evil keeps filing maintenance requests. The story unfolds in The Kingdom Beneath the Extremely Large Hat, where authority increases according to the size of one's ceremonial hat. The central problem is a celestial committee preparing an audit of mortal civilization. Lio Ash wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A dungeon manager tries to reduce adventurer complaints while an ancient evil keeps filing maintenance requests.
authorNotes: Every coincidence is intentional. Every typo is probably a prophecy.

world.name: The Kingdom Beneath the Extremely Large Hat
world.rule: Authority increases according to the size of one's ceremonial hat.
world.oddity: The national treasure is a perfectly ordinary spoon.
world.magic: Magic is powered by unresolved problems; solving one can actually make you weaker.
world.threat: a celestial committee preparing an audit of mortal civilization

chapters.title: My Completely Reasonable Plan To the World's Least Useful Sword — Lio Ash POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Lio Ash POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Lio Ash arrived at the floating warehouse intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
The road changes its destination while everyone is still walking on it.
Lio Ash noticed three details before anyone else noticed the first one.
The important object was a permit. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Lio Ash checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Kingdom Beneath the Extremely Large Hat followed one inconvenient rule: Authority increases according to the size of one's ceremonial hat.
The road bent left, reconsidered, and politely delivered them somewhere else.
The room looked ordinary until the small things started disagreeing with one another.
A second person arrived carrying information about the suspicious invoice. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the permit. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Lio Ash wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Lio Ash has a private connection to the border dispute.
The mystery remained open, although Lio Ash now had one useful fact: someone was treating the suspicious invoice as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Lio Ash made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
